newsitem.title: ITALY: Milan Bourse capitalisation, trade see 1996 record.
newsitem.headline: Milan Bourse capitalisation, trade see 1996 record.

text.p: The Milan stock exchange saw its total market capitalisation rise 17.3 percent in 1996 to an estimated record high of 382.0 trillion lire, the Bourse Council said in a statement.
This compared to growth of 10.9 percent to 325.57 trillion lire in 1995, the Council said with just one day's trading left this year.
Total traded volume also set a record this year, mainly due to strong growth in derivatives, rising to an estimated 630.50 trillion lire from 311.12 trillion lire in 1995.
Fifteen new companies made their Bourse debut in 1996, but taking into account those leaving the market this took the total of companies with shares quoted to 215 against 217 in 1995 and 219 in 1994.
The total nominal capital of listed companies, however, rose to 97.60 trillion lire from 94.76 trillion lire in 1995 and 82.00 trillion in 1994.
Average daily traded share volume rose to 621 billion lire in 1996 against 561.4 billion in 1994, but declined from 757 billion lire seen in 1994.
